# M7 Phase 0 — measured per-kernel hazard attribution

**Goal.** Drive the M7 design (split I/D memory port + a real 1-cycle-hit I-cache,
`PIPELINE_MASTER_PLAN.md` §4.3) from *measured* pipeline-hazard attribution, not
estimates — the "measure before you cut" discipline of the ICACHE handoff Phase 0.

**Instrument.** `haz_probe_*.kla` (generated by `gen_probe.py`): a standalone,
hand-assembled program that reproduces the six `perf_baseline.c` micro-kernels
(same dependency / branch / memory signature) and, per kernel, does
`clear PERF_CTRL → run → snapshot all counters → print`. It reads the M6 pipeline
hazard counters `0xF00D_00B0..00E8` plus cycles (`0x08`) and retired instructions
(`0x10`). A hand-assembled `.kla` (not an edit to `perf_baseline.c`) is the right
instrument: `perf_baseline.elf` is the **pinned A/B baseline** (`perf/METHOD.md`
stale-ELF trap) — recompiling it to add counter reads would perturb the reference.

**Counters** (see `MMIO_MAP.md`): `DATA` GPR-RAW stall, `LOADUSE` load-use subset,
`FLAGS` flag-reader stall, `SP` stack-serialize stall, `MULDIV` EX-busy, `BRFLUSH`
taken-redirect events, `IF_MISS` fetch-window-empty cycles, `MEM_WAIT` MEM-port-busy
cycles. Each hazard number below is that counter as a % of the kernel's cycles.

## Board (Nexys A7, M6 pipeline bitstream, real DDR2) — the numbers that drive M7

| kernel | CPI | DATA | LOADUSE | FLAGS | SP | MULDIV | BRFLUSH | **IF_MISS** | **MEM_WAIT** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| alu        | 3.33 | 16.0% | 0     | 0    | 0    | 0     | 2.0% | **60.0%** | 0.0% |
| mem_stream | 6.51 | 37.5% | 33.1% | 2.2% | 0    | 0     | 2.2% | **43.9%** | **38.6%** |
| ptr_chase  | 7.67 | 62.5% | 56.0% | 1.6% | 0    | 0     | 1.6% | **32.6%** | **54.4%** |
| branchy    | 4.41 |  9.0% | 0     | 0.8% | 0    | 0     | 2.6% | **73.3%** | 0.0% |
| calls_fib  | 7.69 |  4.9% | 4.1%  | 0    | 7.3% | 0     | 2.4% | **53.7%** | **36.6%** |
| muldiv     | 4.18 | 10.1% | 0     | 2.0% | 0    | 14.3% | 2.0% | **59.8%** | 0.0% |

Machine-readable: `haz_attribution_board.csv`. Cross-check: probe **branchy CPI 4.41**
≈ `baseline_m6_pipeline.csv` branchy **4.402** (branchy is compute-bound and
codegen-insensitive) — the probe tracks the real compiled kernel.

### What the data says (the M7 case)

1. **Fetch supply is the dominant bottleneck, everywhere.** `IF_MISS` is the single
   largest hazard class in 5 of 6 kernels (33–73% of all cycles). It is large even
   where there is **zero** memory traffic:
   - `alu`: `MEM_WAIT`=0, only **1 branch per 15 instructions** (200 k branches over
     3 M instrs) — i.e. 93% straight-line — yet **60% IF_MISS**. The front end cannot
     sustain 1 instr/cycle even on cache-resident *straight-line* code. This is a pure
     fetch-**supply** limit (the 2-dword IFB refilled through the shared port, lower
     priority than MEM), not a branch or contention effect.
   - `branchy`: `MEM_WAIT`=0, **73% IF_MISS** — the worst; fetch-supply latency plus
     taken-redirect refill of the tiny IFB.
   → **A dedicated 1-cycle-hit I-cache (its own port, delivers a dword/cycle on a hit)
   directly attacks IF_MISS for every kernel.** This is the biggest single lever.

2. **The memory kernels pay IF_MISS *and* MEM_WAIT, and they overlap.** With one
   shared port, fetch starves whenever MEM holds it:
   - `mem_stream`: IF_MISS 43.9% **+** MEM_WAIT 38.6%
   - `ptr_chase`:  IF_MISS 32.6% **+** MEM_WAIT 54.4%
   - `calls_fib`:  IF_MISS 53.7% **+** MEM_WAIT 36.6% (stack traffic)
   → **A split I/D port lets fetch proceed from the I-cache during data misses**, so
   the IF_MISS and MEM_WAIT components stop serializing. This is the §4.3 lever and it
   pairs with (does not replace) the I-cache.

3. **What M7 does *not* address (context, so we don't over-claim):**
   - `ptr_chase` DATA 62.5% / LOADUSE 56.0% — genuine dependent-load-use latency;
     needs scheduling / non-blocking loads (M8), not fetch.
   - `muldiv` MULDIV 14.3% — inherent multi-cycle EX.
   - `calls_fib` SP 7.3% — stack-serialize; the only SP-stalling kernel (as expected).
   - `BRFLUSH` 1.6–2.6% everywhere — taken-branch redirect events; the residual
     IF_MISS after an I-cache is branch-refill, which needs prediction / back-edge
     layout (later M7 / M8), not the cache.

### Priority order implied by the measurement
1. **1-cycle-hit I-cache with its own fetch port** — collapses IF_MISS (33–73% → branch-
   refill floor) on all six kernels; single biggest win, and helps compute kernels that
   the split-port alone would not.
2. **Split I/D memory port** — removes fetch/data contention so the memory kernels'
   IF_MISS and MEM_WAIT overlap instead of serialize.
   (These two are one milestone: the I-cache *is* the second port.)
3. Later: branch handling (predict / back-edge) for the BRFLUSH residual; load-use
   scheduling for ptr_chase DATA/LOADUSE.

## SoC sim (tb_soc, behavioral DDR, small working sets) — plumbing check only

`haz_attribution_sim.csv`. Confirms the pipeline reads `0xF00D_00B0..E8` correctly and
each kernel's signature is right (muldiv is the only MULDIV-stalling kernel; calls_fib
the only SP-stalling one; IF_MISS < cycles). Magnitudes are the model's fixed 8-cycle
DDR with in-cache working sets — **not** silicon; the board table above is the real one.

## Real-workload hazard attribution (`perf_haz`) — codegen-faithful cross-check

The `.kla` probe reproduces each kernel's *algorithmic* hazard signature but not the
compiler's codegen. `perf_haz.elf` (runtime repo: `baremetal/programs/perf_haz.c`, a
copy of `perf_baseline.c` that also snapshots `0xF00D_00B0..E8` per kernel) runs the
**real compiled kernels with the real 256 KiB working set**. It is its OWN ELF — not
an edit to the pinned `perf_baseline.elf` (which must stay pinned for the CPI A/B).

**M6 board baseline** (`haz_real_m6.csv`, % of cycles):

| kernel | CPI | DATA | LOADUSE | SP | MULDIV | BRFLUSH | **IF_MISS** | **MEM_WAIT** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| alu        | 3.94 | 12.7 | 0.0  | 0    | 0    | 1.6 | **63.5** | 0.0 |
| mem_stream | 7.32 | 19.2 | 17.3 | 0    | 0    | 1.9 | **53.7** | **39.5** |
| ptr_chase  | 5.87 |  7.9 | 0.0  | 0    | 0    | 1.3 | **39.3** | **41.0** |
| branchy    | 4.26 | 10.4 | 0.0  | 0    | 0    | 1.4 | **72.5** | 0.0 |
| calls_fib  | 6.24 |  2.4 | 0.0  | 10.2 | 0    | 1.9 | **58.3** | **31.6** |
| muldiv     | 4.21 |  9.6 | 0.0  | 0    | 11.3 | 1.6 | **71.3** | 0.0 |

**Fidelity vs the micro-kernel probe:** IF_MISS matches well (real vs probe: alu
63.5/60, branchy 72.5/73, mem_stream 53.7/44, muldiv 71.3/60) — so the probe was a
sound proxy for the *design* decision (IF_MISS dominant, 39–73% on real code). But
**LOADUSE diverges**: ptr_chase real **0.0%** vs probe 56%, mem_stream 17.3% vs 33% —
the compiler schedules intervening instructions between a dependent load and its use,
hiding the latency, whereas hand-asm has tight load→use. So `perf_haz` is the vehicle
for the definitive per-kernel impact numbers; run it on the M7 bitstream for the A/B.

## Reproduce
```
# board (needs the M6 pipeline bitstream programmed, e.g. ~/.klausscpu_scratch/prog.tcl)
python3 gen_probe.py board > haz_probe_board.kla
klausscc --input haz_probe_board.kla --serial /dev/ttyUSB1 --monitor 2> board.raw
python3 parse_haz.py board.raw --csv haz_attribution_board.csv

# SoC sim plumbing check
./run_probe_soc.sh sim
```
`kbt2mem.py` converts a klausscc `.kbt` (assembled `.kla`) to a `boot_rom` `$readmemh`
image so tb_soc / tb_pipeline_isa can boot a hand-assembled program (`--mem-out` only
consumes ELF/flat-binary). Verified byte-exact against `--mem-out hello.elf`.
